title: Counit normalization of the site-transported closed adjoint
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $R=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Write $S_T=\nu_T^*$ and $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$ for etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $I=Ri^!_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the ordinary etale closed right adjoint [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and $J=S_Z I U_P$ for the finite transported exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], identifying the etale compact-support adjoint with $I$ by its counit-compatible adjunction comparison. Give $J$ the bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] for the identity-open compactification of $i$. Let $H\in D^+(P_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ and suppose $IH\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R)$. Let $\eta_H:H\xrightarrow{\sim}U_PS_PH$ be the specified comparison unit [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and set
$$\alpha_H=S_ZI(\eta_H):S_ZIH\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_PH.$$
For bounded-below $L$ let $\delta_L:S_Pi_*^{\mathrm{et}}L\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}S_ZL$ be the normalized canonical comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. With $e_H:i_*^{\mathrm{et}}IH\to H$ the etale exceptional counit and $E_{S_PH}:i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}JS_PH\to S_PH$ the transported exceptional counit, one has
$$E_{S_PH}\circ i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_H)\circ\delta_{IH}=S_P(e_H).$$
More generally the transported exceptional adjunct of $S_P(f)\circ\delta_L^{-1}$, for $f:i_*^{\mathrm{et}}L\to H$, is $\alpha_H\circ S_Z(\widehat f)$, where $\widehat f:L\to IH$ is the etale exceptional adjunct.

proof.text: Use the ordinary adjunction F ⊣ G supplied in the statement; no existence theorem or exceptional coefficient system is chosen. The specified site-comparison unit at H is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Its images under G and S_Z give the isomorphism alpha. The exact comparison pullback preserves bounded-below objects [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], so S_Z G H has etale origin; transporting this property along alpha supplies hJ.

source.place: Displayed Hom chain, bounded-below domains; construction of alpha in the extracted closed-immersion calculation

proof.text: Compare fixedCompactSupportComparisonIso with compactSupportSiteComparison [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Expand their definitions, retaining the same canonical proper direct-image mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The inclusions of D+ carry the exact derived composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons to their ambient versions. Naturality of the inverse right-derived inclusion comparison moves the composite of the three open-extension factors across it in one rewrite. Both sides are then the identical composite. Thus the private component calculation proves equality for every compactification, in particular the identity-open compactification c₀. Substitute this equality in C.homEquiv_normalized; it gives precisely the displayed transported Hom chain with delta inverse as its first factor.

proof.text: For f : F L → H, naturality of the specified comparison unit [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies the inverse comparison-adjunction image of f followed by the unit at H with S_P(f). Apply C.homEquiv_normalized and the equality of Step 2. Naturality in the target of the supplied ordinary adjunction gives beta(f followed by eta_H) = beta(f) followed by G(eta_H). Functoriality of S_Z proves the general adjunct formula, without assuming any exceptional-counit equation.

source.place: Displayed Hom chain, applied to the image of an ordinary etale morphism; explicit unit-naturality computation

proof.text: Define E as the inverse image of the identity under C.homEquiv, using hJ from Step 1. Source naturality of the specified relative Hom equivalence [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] says that the transpose of Fpro(alpha) followed by E is alpha. Apply the general formula of Step 3 at L = G H and f the counit of the supplied ordinary adjunction. The transpose of that counit is the identity, so the resulting transpose is also alpha. Injectivity of C.homEquiv identifies the two morphisms. Precompose by delta and cancel delta followed by its inverse to obtain the required counit identity.
